story.iWant: to filter my analytics by specific role (Don, Mafia, Sheriff, Citizen)
story.soThat: I can focus on performance for a single role

tasks.task: Task 1: Create RoleFilter component (AC: #1, #2, #3, #5) - Create `RoleFilter` component in `src/components/analytics/` - Implement multi-select toggle buttons or dropdown for roles (Don, Mafia, Sheriff, Citizen) - Add role selection state management - Implement clear/reset functionality - Add active filter badge display - Connect to Zustand analytics store for filter state - Add smooth animations for filter changes (< 300ms) - Make component responsive (mobile: stacked layout, desktop: horizontal) - Add component tests using React Testing Library

Task 2: Update analytics store to support role filtering (AC: #1, #4) - Update `src/store/analyticsStore.ts` to include `roles` state (array of role strings) - Add `setRoles` action to update selected roles - Add `clearRoles` action to reset role filter - Add `toggleRole` action to add/remove individual roles - Ensure role filter state persists across navigation - Add TypeScript types for RoleFilter (array of 'DON' | 'MAFIA' | 'SHERIFF' | 'CITIZEN') - Add unit tests for store actions

Task 3: Update API endpoints to accept role filter parameters (AC: #1, #2, #3) - Update `GET /api/players/[id]/analytics/role-based` to accept `roles?` query parameter (comma-separated: don,mafia,sheriff,citizen) - Update `GET /api/players/[id]/analytics/elo-trends` to accept `roles?` query parameter - Update `GET /api/players/[id]/analytics/win-rates` to accept `roles?` query parameter - Update `GET /api/players/[id]/analytics/summary` to accept `roles?` query parameter - Update `GET /api/players/[id]/analytics/trends` to accept `roles?` query parameter (if endpoint exists) - Update `GET /api/players/[id]/analytics/role-comparison` to accept `roles?` query parameter (if endpoint exists) - Add Zod validation schemas for role filter query parameters - Add input validation (valid role values, array format) - Add error handling for invalid role filters (400 Bad Request) - Add integration tests for role filtering on all endpoints

Task 4: Update repository layer to filter by role (AC: #1, #2, #3) - Update `role-metrics.repository.ts` to filter games by role(s) - Update `elo-trends.repository.ts` to filter ELO data by role(s) - Update `win-rate.repository.ts` to filter win/loss records by role(s) - Update `performance-summary.repository.ts` to filter summary data by role(s) - Update `trends.repository.ts` to filter trend data by role(s) (if repository exists) - Update `role-comparison.repository.ts` to filter comparison data by role(s) (if repository exists) - Ensure role filtering uses indexed columns (role in GameParticipation) for performance - Add database query optimization (use Prisma WHERE IN clause for multiple roles) - Add unit tests for repository role filtering logic

Task 5: Update analytics components to use role filter (AC: #1, #4, #6) - Update `RoleMetricsDisplay` component to read roles from store and pass to API - Update `ELOTrendsChart` component to read roles from store and pass to API - Update `WinRateAnalysis` component to read roles from store and pass to API - Update `PerformanceSummary` component to read roles from store and pass to API - Update `TrendsChart` component to read roles from store and pass to API (if component exists) - Update `RoleComparison` component to read roles from store and pass to API (if component exists) - Ensure all components trigger data refetch when roles change - Add loading states that respect role filter - Add smooth animations when data updates after filter change (< 300ms) - Update component tests to verify role filtering integration

Task 6: Create role filter utilities and helpers (AC: #1, #2, #3) - Create `src/lib/utils/roleFilter.ts` utility module (if needed) - Implement `formatRoleFilterLabel(roles)` function for display badges - Implement `validateRoleFilter(roles)` function - Add role display name mapping (DON → "Don", MAFIA → "Mafia", etc.) - Add role color/icon mapping for visual indicators - Add unit tests for role filter utilities

Task 7: Add filter indicator component for roles (AC: #1, #4) - Update `FilterIndicator` component to display active role filters - Display active role filter badges ("Don selected", "Mafia + Sheriff selected") - Add clear button to remove role filter(s) - Show loading state when role filter is applied and data is loading - Make indicator responsive and accessible - Integrate into analytics dashboard layout alongside date range filter - Add component tests

Task 8: Integrate RoleFilter into analytics dashboard (AC: #1, #4) - Add `RoleFilter` component to analytics dashboard page - Position filter component prominently (near DateRangeFilter) - Ensure filter state persists across analytics section navigation - Connect filter to all analytics components via Zustand store - Test filter integration with all analytics views - Add responsive layout for filter component

Task 9: Add TypeScript types and interfaces (AC: #1, #2, #3) - Define `Role` type union ('DON' | 'MAFIA' | 'SHERIFF' | 'CITIZEN') - Define `RoleFilter` type (array of Role) - Define `RoleFilterProps` interface - Update `AnalyticsFilters` interface in store to include roles (if not already present) - Add types for API request/response with role filter - Ensure type safety throughout component tree - Add JSDoc comments for all public interfaces

Task 10: Add error handling and edge cases (AC: #3, #6) - Handle invalid role selections (empty array, invalid role values) - Display user-friendly error messages for invalid filters - Handle edge cases (no data for selected role(s), all roles selected) - Add retry logic for failed API calls with role filters (TanStack Query handles retries) - Handle loading states gracefully during filter changes - Handle timezone edge cases (if applicable)

Task 11: Performance optimization (AC: #1, #4) - Implement TanStack Query caching with roles as part of cache key - Optimize database queries with role filters (use indexes) - Optimize component re-renders when role filter changes - Measure and verify performance targets (< 500ms API response, < 300ms filter update) - Add query optimization for role filtering (Prisma WHERE IN clause)

Task 12: Testing (AC: #1, #2, #3, #4, #5, #6) - Unit tests for role filter utilities (if any) - Unit tests for analytics store role filter actions - Integration tests for API endpoints with role filter parameters - Integration tests for repository role filtering - Component tests for `RoleFilter` (single select, multi-select, clear, validation) - Component tests for `FilterIndicator` with role filters (display, clear button, loading state) - Component tests for analytics components with role filtering - E2E test: Complete flow (select single role → verify analytics update → select multiple roles → verify update → clear filter → verify reset)

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Given I am viewing analytics, When I select role filter(s) (Don, Mafia, Sheriff, Citizen), Then the system: Updates all analytics to show data only for selected role(s), Allows multi-select (view multiple roles simultaneously or single role), Shows active filter badges ("Don selected", "Mafia + Sheriff selected"), Refreshes charts and metrics immediately, Clear/Reset filter option available

Given I am viewing analytics, When I select a single role filter (Don, Mafia, Sheriff, or Citizen), Then the system: Updates all analytics views to show data only for the selected role, Displays role-specific metrics, charts, and statistics, Shows active filter badge with role name ("Don selected"), Smoothly transitions analytics data (< 300ms), Maintains filter selection across page navigation

Given I am viewing analytics, When I select multiple role filters (e.g., Don + Mafia), Then the system: Updates all analytics to show aggregated data for selected roles, Combines metrics from selected roles appropriately, Shows active filter badges indicating all selected roles ("Don + Mafia selected"), Charts display combined data for selected roles, Clear option available to remove all role filters

Given I have applied a role filter, When I navigate to different analytics sections (role metrics, ELO trends, win rates, etc.), Then the system: Maintains the active role filter(s) across all sections, All analytics components show data for the same selected role(s), Filter badges remain visible and consistent, Filter state persists across navigation

Given I have applied a role filter, When I clear the role filter, Then the system: Resets to show all roles (no filtering), Updates all analytics components to show unfiltered data, Removes filter badges, Smoothly transitions back to unfiltered view

Given I am viewing analytics with a role filter applied, When the data is loading, Then the system: Shows loading states in all affected analytics components, Displays filter badges with loading state, Maintains filter selection during loading

constraints.constraint: Clean Architecture + Hexagonal Architecture: RoleFilter component in Presentation Layer (`src/components/analytics/`), role filter utilities in Application Layer (`src/lib/utils/`), role filtering in Infrastructure Layer repositories
State Management: Use TanStack Query for server state (analytics data), Zustand for client state (filters). Role filter state in `src/store/analyticsStore.ts` alongside dateRange
Component Library: Use ShadCN/UI ToggleGroup or Select component for role selection with custom styling. Follow DateRangeFilter component pattern
Styling: Use Tailwind CSS 3.3.0 with tailwind-variants for component variants
Type Safety: TypeScript 5.0.0 with strict mode. Maintain type safety throughout. Add Role and RoleFilter types to `src/types/analytics.ts`
Validation: Use Zod 4.1.12 for API request/response validation. Add role filter validation schemas
Performance: API response time < 500ms, filter update < 300ms. Use Prisma WHERE IN clause for multiple roles. Use indexed columns (role in GameParticipation)
Testing: Maintain minimum 80% test coverage. Unit tests (Vitest), component tests (React Testing Library), integration tests, E2E tests (Playwright)
Filter Integration: Filter state managed in Zustand store ensures filter changes trigger data refetch across all analytics components. Role filter should follow same pattern as date range filter
Default Behavior: Default filter state should be `null` or empty array (no filtering) to show all roles. Align with date range filter default behavior
Smooth Animations: Use opacity transitions and skeleton screens for smooth UX during filter changes. Apply same pattern for role filter updates (< 300ms transition)
Authentication: All analytics endpoints require authentication via NextAuth.js session. Role filtering doesn't change auth requirements

ideas.idea: Test multi-select role filtering: Select Don → verify analytics update → Add Mafia → verify combined data → Verify filter badges show both roles → Clear filter → verify reset to all roles
Test single role filter: Select Don → verify all analytics components show Don-only data → Navigate to different sections → verify filter persists → Verify smooth transition (< 300ms)
Test multiple role aggregation: Select Don + Mafia → verify metrics are combined correctly → Verify charts show aggregated data → Verify filter badges display correctly
Test filter persistence: Apply role filter → Navigate between analytics sections → Verify filter state maintained → Verify all components show filtered data
Test clear filter: Apply role filter → Clear filter → Verify all analytics reset to unfiltered view → Verify filter badges removed → Verify smooth transition
Test loading states: Apply role filter → Verify loading indicators show → Verify filter badges show loading state → Verify filter selection maintained during loading
Test invalid role filter: Submit invalid role values → Verify 400 Bad Request error → Verify user-friendly error message displayed
Test empty role filter: Submit empty roles array → Verify shows all roles (no filtering) → Verify no filter badges displayed
Test performance: Measure API response time with role filter (< 500ms target) → Measure filter update latency (< 300ms target) → Verify database query uses indexes
Test edge cases: No data for selected role(s) → Verify empty state displayed → All roles selected → Verify same as no filter → Verify filter works with date range filter combined
